title: Crisp Salt and Pepper Squid with Chilli, Garlic and Spring Onion
summary: Crisp, lightly coated squid is deep-fried until golden, then tossed hot with garlic, chilli, spring onion and a fragrant salt and pepper mix.
equipment: large heavy pot or wok for deep-frying (at least 4 litres)
wire rack set over a tray lined with kitchen paper
large frying pan or second wok

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Dry the Squid
steps.text: Rinse the squid, then spread it over kitchen paper, cover with more paper and press firmly to blot away excess moisture. Leave it for 10 minutes; squid that's properly dried fries up noticeably crisper and spits far less in hot oil.

steps.title: Mix the Salt and Pepper
steps.text: Stir the salt, white pepper and black pepper together in a small bowl and set aside. Having this mix ready means you can season the squid the moment it's fried and still hot, so it sticks and seasons evenly.

steps.title: Heat the Oil
steps.text: Pour the oil into a large heavy pot, filling it no more than a third full, and heat over medium-high heat to 180°C, checking with a thermometer. Keeping the oil at a steady 180°C gives a crisp, pale golden coating without the squid turning greasy or burning before it's cooked through.

steps.title: Coat and Fry in Batches
steps.text: Mix the cornflour, plain flour and salt together, then toss a third of the squid through it, shaking off the excess. Lower it into the oil piece by piece so it doesn't clump, and fry for 1.5-2 minutes until pale golden, crisp and opaque all the way through; cooking it any longer turns squid rubbery rather than tender. Lift onto a wire rack, let the oil return to 180°C, and fry the rest in two more batches.

steps.title: Toss with Garlic and Chilli
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp of oil in a frying pan over medium heat, add the garlic and chillies and stir for about a minute until fragrant and the garlic is just turning golden. Take the pan off the heat, add the fried squid and spring onions, sprinkle over the salt and pepper mix and toss well so every piece is coated.

steps.title: Serve Hot
steps.text: Pile the squid onto a plate and serve immediately with lime wedges for squeezing over. It's best eaten hot and crisp straight from the pan, before the coating has a chance to soften.

tips: Dry the squid thoroughly before coating it — any surface moisture stops the coating turning properly crisp and causes the oil to spit.
A common mistake is overcrowding the fryer; add the squid a piece at a time and fry in batches so the oil temperature doesn't drop and the coating stays crisp.
Watch the clock closely — squid cooked much beyond 2 minutes turns tough and rubbery rather than tender.
safety: Never leave hot oil unattended, and let it cool completely before moving or disposing of it.
storage: Salt and pepper squid is best eaten fresh, as the coating softens on standing. If needed, keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 1 day and reheat in a hot oven or air fryer until piping hot (74°C) and crisp again; avoid the microwave, which will make the coating soggy. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
